<h1 id="orders">Orders v2.32</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

An order represents a payment between two or more parties. Use the Orders API to create, update, retrieve, authorize, and capture orders.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api-m.paypal.com">https://api-m.paypal.com</a> - Server for https scheme.

<a href="../doc/USERGUIDE.md">External documentation</a>

# Authentication

- oAuth2 authentication. Oauth 2.0 authentication

    - Flow: clientCredentials
    - Token URL = [https://api-m.paypal.com/v1/oauth2/token](https://api-m.paypal.com/v1/oauth2/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/payment|Manage payments and checkout workflow.|
|https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/payment/reference-transaction|Permission to initiate reference transaction|
|https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/initiatepayment|Initiates payments and checkout workflows.|
|https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/orders/deprecating-jssdk-migration-for-limited-merchants|Allows client-side integration on Create, Get, Patch, Authorize & Capture Order endpoints.|
|https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/orders/client_sdk_orders_api|Enables secure client-side integration on confirm payment source endpoint|
|https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/orders/provision-card|Manage card provisioning merchants.|

<h1 id="orders-externalcallback">externalcallback</h1>

PayPal will use the callback url defined in the create order request to send merchants shipping address and shipping options data while the buyer is in the PayPal checkout.

## Receive updated order information via callback URL

<a id="opIdserver.callback"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-m.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders/order-update-callback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "5O190127TN364715T",
    "shipping_address": {
      "country_code": "US",
      "admin_area_1": "TX",
      "admin_area_2": "Dallas",
      "postal_code": "75001"
    },
    "purchase_units": [
      {
        "reference_id": "d9f80740-38f0-11e8-b467-0ed5f89f718b",
        "amount": {
          "currency_code": "USD",
          "value": "100.00",
          "breakdown": {
            "item_total": {
              "currency_code": "USD",
              "value": "90.00"
            },
            "tax_total": {
              "currency_code": "USD",
              "value": "10.00"
            },
            "shipping": {
              "currency_code": "USD",
              "value": "0.00"
            }
          }
        },
        "items": [
          {
            "name": "T-Shirt",
            "description": "Green XL",
            "sku": "sku01",
            "unit_amount": {
              "currency_code": "USD",
              "value": "90.00"
            },
            "tax": {
              "currency_code": "USD",
              "value": "10.00"
            },
            "quantity": "1",
            "category": "PHYSICAL_GOODS"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/checkout/orders/order-update-callback`

The documentation for this 'endpoint' is different from the other endpoints under v2 Orders. For this endpoint the role of client and server is reversed. The client sending the request is PayPal, and the server sending the response is the merchant. In the request, PayPal will send the buyer's redacted shipping address and selected shipping option to the callback URL defined the create order request. The response from the merchant will update the Orders resource.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "5O190127TN364715T",
  "shipping_address": {
    "country_code": "US",
    "admin_area_1": "TX",
    "admin_area_2": "Dallas",
    "postal_code": "75001"
  },
  "purchase_units": [
    {
      "reference_id": "d9f80740-38f0-11e8-b467-0ed5f89f718b",
      "amount": {
        "currency_code": "USD",
        "value": "100.00",
        "breakdown": {
          "item_total": {
            "currency_code": "USD",
            "value": "90.00"
          },
          "tax_total": {
            "currency_code": "USD",
            "value": "10.00"
          },
          "shipping": {
            "currency_code": "USD",
            "value": "0.00"
          }
        }
      },
      "items": [
        {
          "name": "T-Shirt",
          "description": "Green XL",
          "sku": "sku01",
          "unit_amount": {
            "currency_code": "USD",
            "value": "90.00"
          },
          "tax": {
            "currency_code": "USD",
            "value": "10.00"
          },
          "quantity": "1",
          "category": "PHYSICAL_GOODS"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Oauth2 ( Scopes: https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/payment )

<h1 id="orders-orders">orders</h1>

Use the `/orders` resource to create, update, retrieve, authorize, capture and track orders.

## Create order

<a id="opIdorders.create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-m.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "payment_source": {

        }
      }
    },

          "currency_code": "USD",
          "value": "230.00",
          "breakdown": {

              "currency_code": "USD",
              "value": "220.00"
            },
            "shipping": {
              "currency_code": "USD",
              "value": "10.00"
            }
          }
        },
        "items": [
          {
            "name": "T-Shirt",
            "description": "Super Fresh Shirt",
            "unit_amount": {
              "currency_code": "USD",
              "value": "20.00"
            },
            "quantity": "1",
            "category": "PHYSICAL_GOODS",
            "sku": "sku01",
            "image_url": "https://example.com/static/images/items/1/tshirt_green.jpg",
            "url": "https://example.com/url-to-the-item-being-purchased-1",
            "upc": {

              "code": "123456789012"
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "Shoes",
            "description": "Running, Size 10.5",
            "sku": "sku02",
            "unit_amount": {
              "currency_code": "USD",
              "value": "100.00"
```

`POST /v2/checkout/orders`

Creates an order. Merchants and partners can add Level 2 and 3 data to payments to reduce risk and payment processing costs. For more information about processing payments, see <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/docs/checkout/advanced/processing/">checkout</a> or <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/docs/multiparty/checkout/advanced/processing/">multiparty checkout</a>.<blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> For error handling and troubleshooting, see <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/reference/orders/v2/errors/#create-order">Orders v2 errors</a>.</blockquote>

<h3 id="create-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|PayPal-Request-Id|header|string|false|The server stores keys for 6 hours. The API callers can request the times to up to 72 hours by speaking to their Account Manager. It is mandatory for all single-step create order calls (E.g. Create Order Request with payment source information like Card, PayPal.vault_id, PayPal.billing_agreement_id, etc).|
|PayPal-Partner-Attribution-Id|header|string|false|PayPal Partner can send a PayPal-Partner-Attribution-Id request header with the value that they have been assigned by the PayPal Partner program. This value is known as a BN Code. In order to reward such partners (through partner programs), all the activities (including API calls) that they are doing on behalf of the merchants need to be tracked.|
|PayPal-Client-Metadata-Id|header|[guid](#schemaguid)|false|A GUID value originating from Fraudnet and Dyson passed from external API clients via HTTP header. The value is used by Risk decisions to correlate calls which, in turn, might result in lower decline rates..|
|Prefer|header|string|false|The preferred server response upon successful completion of the request. Value is:<ul><li><code>return=minimal</code>. The server returns a minimal response to optimize communication between the API caller and the server. A minimal response includes the <code>id</code>, <code>status</code> and HATEOAS links.</li><li><code>return=representation</code>. The server returns a complete resource representation, including the current state of the resource.</li></ul>|
|Authorization|header|[standard_header_schema](#schemastandard_header_schema)|false|Holds authorization information for external API calls.|
|PayPal-Auth-Assertion|header|string|false|Header for an API client-provided JWT assertion that identifies the merchant. Establishing the consent to act-on-behalf of a merchant is a prerequisite for using this header.|

## Show order details

<a id="opIdorders.get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-m.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders/5O190127TN364715T \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/checkout/orders/{id}`

Shows details for an order, by ID.<blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> For error handling and troubleshooting, see <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/reference/orders/v2/errors/#get-order">Orders v2 errors</a>.</blockquote>

<h3 id="show-order-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the order for which to show details.|
|Authorization|header|[standard_header_schema](#schemastandard_header_schema)|false|Holds authorization information for external API calls.|
|PayPal-Auth-Assertion|header|string|false|Header for an API client-provided JWT assertion that identifies the merchant. Establishing the consent to act-on-behalf of a merchant is a prerequisite for using this header.|
|fields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields that should be returned for the order. Valid filter field is `payment_source`.|

## Update order

<a id="opIdorders.patch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-m.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders/5O190127TN364715T \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "path": "/purchase_units/@reference_id=='\''PUHF'\''/shipping/address",
      "value": {
        "address_line_1": "2211 N First Street",
        "address_line_2": "Building 17",
        "admin_area_2": "San Jose",
        "admin_area_1": "CA",
        "postal_code": "95131",
        "country_code": "US"
      }
    }
  ]'
```

`PATCH /v2/checkout/orders/{id}`

Updates an order with a `CREATED` or `APPROVED` status. You cannot update an order with the `COMPLETED` status.<br/><br/>To make an update, you must provide a `reference_id`. If you omit this value with an order that contains only one purchase unit, PayPal sets the value to `default` which enables you to use the path: <code>\"/purchase_units/@reference_id=='default'/{attribute-or-object}\"</code>. Merchants and partners can add Level 2 and 3 data to payments to reduce risk and payment processing costs. For more information about processing payments, see <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/docs/checkout/advanced/processing/">checkout</a> or <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/docs/multiparty/checkout/advanced/processing/">multiparty checkout</a>.<blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> For error handling and troubleshooting, see <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/reference/orders/v2/errors/#patch-order">Orders v2 errors</a>.</blockquote>Patchable attributes or objects:<br/><br/><table><thead><th>Attribute</th><th>Op</th><th>Notes</th></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>intent</code></td><td>replace</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>payer</code></td><td>replace, add</td><td>Using replace op for <code>payer</code> will replace the whole <code>payer</code> object with the value sent in request.</td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units</code></td><td>replace, add</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].custom_id</code></td><td>replace, add, remove</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].description</code></td><td>replace, add, remove</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].payee.email</code></td><td>replace</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].shipping.name</code></td><td>replace, add</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].shipping.email_address</code></td><td>replace, add</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].shipping.phone_number</code></td><td>replace, add</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].shipping.options</code></td><td>replace, add</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].shipping.address</code></td><td>replace, add</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].shipping.type</code></td><td>replace, add</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>purchase_units[].soft_descriptor</code></td><td>replace, ## Confirm the Order

<a id="opIdorders.confirm"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-m.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders/5O190127TN364715T/confirm-payment-source \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "payment_source": {
      "paypal": {
        "name": {
          "given_name": "John",
          "surname": "Doe"
        },
        "email_address": "customer@example.com",
        "experience_context": {
          "payment_method_preference": "IMMEDIATE_PAYMENT_REQUIRED",
          "brand_name": "EXAMPLE INC",
          "locale": "en-US",
          "landing_page": "LOGIN",
          "shipping_preference": "SET_PROVIDED_ADDRESS",
          "user_action": "PAY_NOW",
          "return_url": "https://example.com/returnUrl",
          "cancel_url": "https://example.com/cancelUrl"
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/checkout/orders/{id}/confirm-payment-source`

```json
        "user_action": "PAY_NOW",

        "cancel_url": "https://example.com/cancelUrl"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Authorize payment for order

<a id="opIdorders.authorize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-m.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders/5O190127TN364715T/authorize \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v2/checkout/orders/{id}/authorize`

Authorizes payment for an order. To successfully authorize payment for an order, the buyer must first approve the order or a valid payment_source must be provided in the request. A buyer can approve the order upon being redirected to the rel:approve URL that was returned in the HATEOAS links in the create order response.<blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> For error handling and troubleshooting, see <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/reference/orders/v2/errors/#authorize-order">Orders v2 errors</a>.</blockquote>

> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="authorize-payment-for-order-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A successful response to an idempotent request returns the HTTP `200 OK` status code with a JSON response body that shows authorized payment details.|[order_authorize_response](#schemaorder_authorize_response)|
|201|Created|A successful response to a non-idempotent request returns the HTTP `201 Created` status code with a JSON response body that shows authorized payment details. If a duplicate response is retried, returns the HTTP `200 OK` status code. By default, the response is minimal. If you need the complete resource representation, you must pass the <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/docs/api/orders/v2/#orders-authorize-header-parameters"><code>Prefer: return=representation</code> request header</a>.|[order_authorize_response](#schemaorder_authorize_response)|
|202|Accepted|The request has been accepted for processing, but the processing has not been completed yet. The server returns the HTTP `202 Accepted` status code to indicate that the request is valid and will be handled asynchronously.|[order_authorize_response](#schemaorder_authorize_response)|
|207|Multi-Status|The request was successfully processed, but the result contains mixed outcomes. When an order includes multiple purchase units, the server returns the HTTP `207 Multi-Status` code to indicate that one or more purchase units were processed successfully while others failed. The response body provides the processing result for each purchase unit.|[order_authorize_response](#schemaorder_authorize_response)|
|400|Bad Request|Request is not well-formed, syntactically incorrect, or violates schema.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the resource. The HTTP `409 Conflict` status code is returned when the requested operation is not allowed because the order or one or more purchase units are in a state that prevents the operation.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The requested action could not be performed, semantically incorrect, or failed business validation.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Default response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Oauth2 ( Scopes: https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/payment https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/orders/deprecating-jssdk-migration-for-limited-merchants )
</aside>

## Capture payment for order

<a id="opIdorders.capture"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-m.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders/5O190127TN364715T/capture \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v2/checkout/orders/{id}/capture`

Captures payment for an order. To successfully capture payment for an order, the buyer must first approve the order or a valid payment_source must be provided in the request. A buyer can approve the order upon being redirected to the rel:approve URL that was returned in the HATEOAS links in the create order response.<blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> For error handling and troubleshooting, see <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/reference/orders/v2/errors/#capture-order">Orders v2 errors</a>.</blockquote>

> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="capture-payment-for-order-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A successful response to an idempotent request returns the HTTP `200 OK` status code with a JSON response body that shows captured payment details.|[order](#schemaorder)|
|201|Created|A successful response to a non-idempotent request returns the HTTP `201 Created` status code with a JSON response body that shows captured payment details. If a duplicate response is retried, returns the HTTP `200 OK` status code. By default, the response is minimal. If you need the complete resource representation, pass the <a href="https://developer.paypal.com/docs/api/orders/v2/#orders-authorize-header-parameters"><code>Prefer: return=representation</code> request header</a>.|[order](#schemaorder)|
|202|Accepted|The request has been accepted for processing, but the processing has not been completed yet. The server returns the HTTP `202 Accepted` status code to indicate that the request is valid and will be handled asynchronously.|[order](#schemaorder)|
|207|Multi-Status|The request was successfully processed, but the result contains mixed outcomes. When an order includes multiple purchase units, the server returns the HTTP `207 Multi-Status` code to indicate that one or more purchase units were processed successfully while others failed. The response body provides the processing result for each purchase unit.|[order](#schemaorder)|
|400|Bad Request|Request is not well-formed, syntactically incorrect, or violates schema.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the resource. The HTTP `409 Conflict` status code is returned when the requested operation is not allowed because the order or one or more purchase units are in a state that prevents the operation.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The requested action could not be performed, semantically incorrect, or failed business validation.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Default response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Oauth2 ( Scopes: https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/payment https://uri.paypal.com/services/payments/orders/deprecating-jssdk-migration-for-limited-merchants )
</aside>

## Add tracking information for an Order.

<a id="opIdorders.track.create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-m.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders/5O190127TN364715T/track \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "capture_id": "8MC585209K746392H",
    "tracking_number": "443844607820",
    "notify_payer": false,
    "items": [
      {
        "name": "T-Shirt",
        "sku": "sku02",
        "quantity": "1",
        "upc": {
          "type": "UPC-A",
          "code": "012345678901"
        },
        "image_url": "https://www.example.com/example.jpg",
        "url": "https://www.example.com/example"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/checkout/orders/{id}/track`

Adds tracking information for an Order.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "capture_id": "8MC585209K746392H",
  "tracking_number": "443844607820",
  "notify_payer": false,
  "items": [
    {
      "name": "T-Shirt",
      "sku": "sku02",
      "quantity": "1",
      "upc": {
        "type": "UPC-A",
        "code": "012345678901"
      },
      "image_url": "https://www.example.com/example.jpg",
      "url": "https://www.example.com/example"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-tracking-information-for-an-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the order that the tracking information is associated with.|
|Authorization|header|[standard_header_schema](#schemastandard_header_schema)|false|Holds authorization information for external API calls.|
|PayPal-Auth-Assertion|header|string|false|Header for an API client-provided JWT assertion that identifies the merchant. Establishing the consent to act-on-behalf of a merchant is a prerequisite for using this header.|
|body|body|[order_tracker_request](#schemaorder_tracker_request)|true|none|
|» tracking_number|body|string|true|The tracking number for the shipment. This property supports Unicode.|
|» carrier|body|[shipment_carrier](#schemashipment_carrier)|true|The carrier for the shipment. Some carriers have a global version as well as local subsidiaries. The subsidiaries are repeated over many countries and might also have an entry in the global list. Choose the carrier for your country. If the carrier is not available for your country, choose the global version of the carrier. If your carrier name is not in the list, set `carrier` to `OTHER` and set carrier name in `carrier_name_other`. For allowed values, see <a href="/docs/tracking/reference/carriers/">Carriers</a>.|
|» carrier_name_other|body|string|false|The name of the carrier for the shipment. Provide this value only if the carrier parameter is OTHER. This property supports Unicode.|
|» capture_id|body|string|true|The PayPal capture ID.|
|» notify_payer|body|boolean|false|If true, PayPal will send an email notification to the payer of the PayPal transaction. The email contains the tracking details provided through the Orders tracking API request. Independent of any value passed for `notify_payer`, the payer may receive tracking notifications within the PayPal app, based on the user's notification preferences.|
|» items|body|[object]|false|An array of details of items in the shipment.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The item name or title.|
|» » quantity|body|string|false|The item quantity. Must be a whole number.|
|» » sku|body|string|false|The stock keeping unit (SKU) for the item. This can contain unicode characters.|
|» » url|body|string(uri)|false|The URL to the item being purchased. Visible to buyer and used in buyer experiences.|
|» » image_url|body|string(uri)|false|The URL of the item's image. File type and size restrictions apply. An image that violates these restrictions will not be honored.|
|» » upc|body|object|false|none|
|» » » type|body|string|true|The Universal Product Code type.|
|» » » code|body|string|true|The UPC product code of the item.|

<h1 id="orders-trackers">trackers</h1>

Use the `/trackers` resource to update and retrieve tracking information for PayPal orders.

## Update or cancel tracking information for an order

<a id="opIdorders.trackers.patch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-m.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders/5O190127TN364715T/trackers/8MC585209K746392H443844607820 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "op": "add",
      "path": "/notify_payer",
      "value": true
    }
  ]'
```

`PATCH /v2/checkout/orders/{id}/trackers/{tracker_id}`

Updates or cancels the tracking information for a PayPal order, by ID. Updatable attributes or objects:<br/><br/><table><thead><th>Attribute</th><th>Op</th><th>Notes</th></thead><tbody></tr><tr><td><code>items</code></td><td>replace</td><td>Using replace op for <code>items</code> will replace the entire <code>items</code> object with the value sent in request.</td></tr><tr><td><code>notify_payer</code></td><td>replace, add</td><td></td></tr><tr><td><code>status</code></td><td>replace</td><td>Only patching status to CANCELLED is currently supported.</td></tr></tbody></table>

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "op": "add",
    "path": "/notify_payer",
    "value": true
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-or-cancel-tracking-information-for-an-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the order that the tracking information is associated with.|
|tracker_id|path|string|true|The order tracking ID.|
|Authorization|header|[standard_header_schema](#schemastandard_header_schema)|false|Holds authorization information for external API calls.|
|PayPal-Auth-Assertion|header|string|false|Header for an API client-provided JWT assertion that identifies the merchant. Establishing the consent to act-on-behalf of a merchant is a prerequisite for using this header.|
|body|body|[patch_request](#schemapatch_request)|false|none|
|» op|body|string|true|The operation.|
|» path|body|string|false|The <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901">JSON Pointer</a> to the target document location at which to complete the operation.|
|» value|body|object|false|The value to apply. The <code>remove</code>, <code>copy</code>, and <code>move</code> operations do not require a value. Since <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6902">JSON Patch</a> allows any type for <code>value</code>, the <code>type</code> property is not specified.|
|» from|body|string|false|The <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901">JSON Pointer</a> to the target document location from which to move the value. Required for the <code>move</code> operation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» op|add|
|» op|remove|
|» op|replace|
|» op|move|
|» op|copy|
|» op|test|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|prefix|string|false|none|The prefix, or title, to the party's name.|
|given_name|string|false|none|When the party is a person, the party's given, or first, name.|
|surname|string|false|none|When the party is a person, the party's surname or family name. Also known as the last name. Required when the party is a person. Use also to store multiple surnames including the matronymic, or mother's, surname.|
|middle_name|string|false|none|When the party is a person, the party's middle name. Use also to store multiple middle names including the patronymic, or father's, middle name.|
|suffix|string|false|none|The suffix for the party's name.|
|full_name|string|false|none|When the party is a person, the party's full name.|

<h2 id="tocS_date_no_time">date_no_time</h2>

<a id="schema_date_no_time"></a>
<a id="tocSdate_no_time"></a>
<a id="tocsdate_no_time"></a>

```json
"stringstri"
```

The stand-alone date, in [Internet date and time format](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339#section-5.6). To represent special legal values, such as a date of birth, you should use dates with no associated time or time-zone data. Whenever possible, use the standard `date_time` type. This regular expression does not validate all dates. For example, February 31 is valid and nothing is known about leap years.

<h2 id="tocS_country_code">country_code</h2>

<a id="schema_country_code"></a>
<a id="tocScountry_code"></a>
<a id="tocscountry_code"></a>

```json
"st"
```

The [2-character ISO 3166-1 code](/api/rest/reference/country-codes/) that identifies the country or region.<blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> The country code for Great Britain is <code>GB</code> and not <code>UK</code> as used in the top-level domain names for that country. Use the `C2` country code for China worldwide for comparable uncontrolled price (CUP) method, bank card, and cross-border transactions.</blockquote>

<h2 id="tocS_address_portable">address_portable</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaddress_portable"></a>
<a id="schema_address_portable"></a>
<a id="tocSaddress_portable"></a>
<a id="tocsaddress_portable"></a>

```json
{
  "address_line_1": "string",
  "address_line_2": "string",
  "address_line_3": "string",
  "admin_area_4": "string",
  "admin_area_3": "string",
  "admin_area_2": "string",
  "admin_area_1": "string",
  "postal_code": "string",
  "country_code": "st",
  "address_details": {
    "street_number": "string",
    "street_name": "string",
    "street_type": "string",
    "delivery_service": "string",
    "building_name": "string",
    "sub_building": "string"
  }
}
```

The portable international postal address. Maps to [AddressValidationMetadata](https://github.com/googlei18n/libaddressinput/wiki/AddressValidationMetadata) and HTML 5.1 [Autofilling form controls: the autocomplete attribute](https://www.w3.org/TR/html51/sec-forms.html#autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address_line_1|string|false|none|The first line of the address, such as number and street, for example, `173 Drury Lane`. Needed for data entry, and Compliance and Risk checks. This field needs to pass the full address.|
|address_line_2|string|false|none|The second line of the address, for example, a suite or apartment number.|
|address_line_3|string|false|none|The third line of the address, if needed. Examples include a street complement for Brazil, direction text, such as `next to Walmart`, or a landmark in an Indian address.|
|admin_area_4|string|false|none|The neighborhood, ward, or district. This is smaller than `admin_area_level_3` or `sub_locality`. Value is:<ul><li>The postal sorting code that is used in Guernsey and many French territories, such as French Guiana.</li><li>The fine-grained administrative levels in China.</li></ul>|
|admin_area_3|string|false|none|The sub-locality, suburb, neighborhood, or district. This is smaller than `admin_area_level_2`. Value is:<ul><li>Brazil. Suburb, *bairro*, or neighborhood.</li><li>India. Sub-locality or district. Street name information isn't always available, but a sub-locality or district can be a very small area.</li></ul>|
|admin_area_2|string|false|none|A city, town, or village. Smaller than `admin_area_level_1`.|
|admin_area_1|string|false|none|The highest-level sub-division in a country, which is usually a province, state, or ISO-3166-2 subdivision. This data is formatted for postal delivery, for example, `CA` and not `California`. Value, by country, is:<ul><li>UK. A county.</li><li>US. A state.</li><li>Canada. A province.</li><li>Japan. A prefecture.</li><li>Switzerland. A *kanton*.</li></ul>|
|postal_code|string|false|none|The postal code, which is the ZIP code or equivalent. Typically required for countries with a postal code or an equivalent. See [postal code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postal_code).|
|country_code|[country_code](#schemacountry_code)|true|none|The [2-character ISO 3166-1 code](/api/rest/reference/country-codes/) that identifies the country or region.<blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> The country code for Great Britain is <code>GB</code> and not <code>UK</code> as used in the top-level domain names for that country. Use the `C2` country code for China worldwide for comparable uncontrolled price (CUP) method, bank card, and cross-border transactions.</blockquote>|
|address_details|object|false|none|The non-portable additional address details include fine-grain address information for Compliance, Risk, and other scenarios. This isn't portable with common third-party and open source applications. This can include data that is redundant with core fields. For example, `address_portable.address_line_1` is usually a combination of `address_details.street_number`, `street_name`, and `street_type`.|

<h2 id="tocS_amount_with_breakdown">amount_with_breakdown</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaamount_with_breakdown"></a>
<a id="schema_amount_with_breakdown"></a>
<a id="tocSamount_with_breakdown"></a>
<a id="tocsamount_with_breakdown"></a>

```json
{
  "currency_code": "str",
  "value": "string",
  "breakdown": {
    "item_total": {
      "currency_code": "str",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "shipping": {
      "currency_code": "str",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "handling": {
      "currency_code": "str",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "tax_total": {
      "currency_code": "str",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "insurance": {
      "currency_code": "str",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "shipping_discount": {
      "currency_code": "str",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "discount": {
      "currency_code": "str",
      "value": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

The total order amount with an optional breakdown that provides details, such as the total item amount, total tax amount, shipping, handling, insurance, and discounts, if any.<br/>If you specify `amount.breakdown`, the amount equals `item_total` plus `tax_total` plus `shipping` plus `handling` plus `insurance` minus `shipping_discount` minus discount.<br/>The amount must be a positive number. For listed of supported currencies and decimal precision, see the PayPal REST APIs <a href="/docs/integration/direct/rest/currency-codes/">Currency Codes</a>.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|currency_code|[currency_code](#schemacurrency_code)|true|none|The [three-character ISO-4217 currency code](/api/rest/reference/currency-codes/) that identifies the currency.|
|value|string|true|none|The value, which might be:<ul><li>An integer for currencies like `JPY` that are not typically fractional.</li><li>A decimal fraction for currencies like `TND` that are subdivided into thousandths.</li></ul>For the required number of decimal places for a currency code, see [Currency Codes](/api/rest/reference/currency-codes/).|
|breakdown|[amount_breakdown](#schemaamount_breakdown)|false|none|The breakdown of the amount. Breakdown provides details such as total item amount, total tax amount, shipping, handling, insurance, and discounts, if any.|

```json
    "price": {

      "value": "string"
    },
```

The billing cycle providing details of the billing frequency, amount, duration and if the billing cycle is a free, discounted or regular billing cycle. The sequence of the billing cycle will be in the following order - free trial billing cycle(s), discounted trial billing cycle(s), regular billing cycle(s).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenure_type|string|true|none|The tenure type of the billing cycle identifies if the billing cycle is a trial(free or discounted) or regular billing cycle.|
|pricing_scheme|object|false|none|none|
|total_cycles|integer|false|none|The number of times this billing cycle gets executed. |sequence|integer|false|none|The order in which this cycle is to run among other billing cycles. For example, a trial billing cycle has a `sequence` of `1` while a regular billing cycle has a `sequence` of `2`, so that trial cycle runs before the regular cycle.|

The purchase unit request. Includes required information for the payment contract.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|reference_id|string|false|none|The API caller-provided external ID for the purchase unit. Required for multiple purchase units when you must update the order through `PATCH`. If you omit this value and the order contains only one purchase unit, PayPal sets this value to `default`.|
|amount|object|true|none|none|
|payee|object|false|none|none|
|payment_instruction|[payment_instruction](#schemapayment_instruction)|false|none|Any additional payment instructions to be consider during payment processing. This processing instruction is applicable for Capturing an order or Authorizing an Order.|
|description|string|false|none|<blockquote>This field supports up to 3,000 characters, but <strong>any content beyond 127 characters (including spaces) will be truncated. The 127 character limit is reflected in the response</strong> representation of this field.</blockquote>The purchase description. The maximum length of the character is dependent on the type of characters used. The character length is specified assuming a US ASCII character. Depending on type of character; (e.g. accented character, Japanese characters) the number of characters that that can be specified as input might not equal the permissible max length.|
|custom_id|string|false|none|The API caller-provided external ID. Used to reconcile client transactions with PayPal transactions. Appears in transaction and settlement reports but is not visible to the payer.|
|invoice_id|string|false|none|The API caller-provided external invoice number for this order. Appears in both the payer's transaction history and the emails that the payer receives. invoice_id values are required to be unique within each merchant account by default. Although the uniqueness validation is configurable, disabling this behavior will remove the account's ability to use invoice_id in other APIs as an identifier. It is highly recommended to keep a unique invoice_id for each Order.|
|soft_descriptor|string|false|none|<blockquote>This field supports up to 127 characters, but <strong>any content beyond 22 characters (including spaces) will be truncated. The 22 character limit is reflected in the response</strong> representation of this field.</blockquote>The soft descriptor is the dynamic text used to construct the statement descriptor that appears on a payer's card statement.<br><br>If an Order is paid using the "PayPal Wallet", the statement descriptor will appear in following format on the payer's card statement: <code><var>PAYPAL_prefix</var>+(space)+<var>merchant_descriptor</var>+(space)+ <var>soft_descriptor</var></code><blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> The merchant descriptor is the descriptor of the merchant’s payment receiving preferences which can be seen by logging into the merchant account https://www.sandbox.paypal.com/businessprofile/settings/info/edit</blockquote>The <code>PAYPAL</code> prefix uses 8 characters. Only the first 22 characters will be displayed in the statement. <br>For example, if:<ul><li>The PayPal prefix toggle is <code>PAYPAL *</code>.</li><li>The merchant descriptor in the profile is <code>Janes Gift</code>.</li><li>The soft descriptor is <code>800-123-1234</code>.</li></ul>Then, the statement descriptor on the card is <code>PAYPAL * Janes Gift 80</code>.|
|items|[object]|false|none|An array of items that the customer purchases from the merchant.|
|shipping|object|false|none|none|
|supplementary_data|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_language">language</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalanguage"></a>
<a id="schema_language"></a>
<a id="tocSlanguage"></a>
<a id="tocslanguage"></a>

```json
"string"
```

The [language tag](https://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47#section-2) for the language in which to localize the error-related strings, such as messages, issues, and suggested actions. The tag is made up of the [ISO 639-2 language code](https://www.loc.gov/standards/iso639-2/php/code_list.php), the optional [ISO-15924 script tag](https://www.unicode.org/iso15924/codelists.html), and the [ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code](/api/rest/reference/country-codes/) or [M49 region code](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/methodology/m49/).

```json
}
```

Reference values used by the card network to identify a transaction.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Transaction reference id returned by the scheme. For Visa and Amex, this is the "Tran id" field in response. For MasterCard, this is the "BankNet reference id" field in response. For Discover, this is the "NRID" field in response. The pattern we expect for this field from Visa/Amex/CB/Discover is numeric, Mastercard/BNPP is alphanumeric and Paysecure is alphanumeric with special character -.|
|date|string|false|none|The date that the transaction was authorized by the scheme. This field may not be returned for all networks. MasterCard refers to this field as "BankNet reference date". For some specific networks, such as MasterCard and Discover, this date field is mandatory when the `previous_network_transaction_reference_id` is passed.|
|network|object|false|none|none|
|acquirer_reference_number|string|false|none|Reference ID issued for the card transaction. This ID can be used to track the transaction across processors, card brands and issuing banks.|

```json
  "payment_type": "ONE_TIME",
  "usage": "DERIVED",

    "id": "stringstr",
    "date": "stri",
    "network": {},
    "acquirer_reference_number": "string"
  }
}
```

Provides additional details to process a payment using a `card` that has been stored or is intended to be stored (also referred to as stored_credential or card-on-file).<br/>Parameter compatibility:<br/><ul><li>`payment_type=ONE_TIME` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`usage=FIRST` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`previous_transaction_reference` or `previous_network_transaction_reference` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=MERCHANT`.</li><li>Only one of the parameters - `previous_transaction_reference` and `previous_network_transaction_reference` - can be present in the request.</li></ul>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_initiator|[payment_initiator](#schemapayment_initiator)|true|none|The person or party who initiated or triggered the payment.|
|payment_type|[stored_payment_source_payment_type](#schemastored_payment_source_payment_type)|true|none|Indicates the type of the stored payment_source payment.|
|usage|[stored_payment_source_usage_type](#schemastored_payment_source_usage_type)|false|none|Indicates if this is a `first` or `subsequent` payment using a stored payment source (also referred to as stored credential or card on file).|
|previous_network_transaction_reference|[network_transaction_reference](#schemanetwork_transaction_reference)|false|none|Reference values used by the card network to identify a transaction.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|payment_initiator|MERCHANT|
|payment_type|ONE_TIME|
|payment_type|RECURRING|
|payment_type|UNSCHEDULED|
|usage|FIRST|
|usage|SUBSEQUENT|
|usage|DERIVED|

```json
{
  "brand_name": "string",
  "locale": {},
  "shipping_preference": "GET_FROM_FILE",
  "contact_preference": "NO_CONTACT_INFO",
  "return_url": {},
  "cancel_url": {},
  "app_switch_context": {
    "native_app": {
      "os_type": "ANDROID",
      "os_version": "string"
    },
    "mobile_web": {
      "return_flow": "AUTO",
      "buyer_user_agent": "string"
    }
  },
  "landing_page": "NO_PREFERENCE",
  "user_action": "CONTINUE",
  "payment_method_preference": "UNRESTRICTED",
  "order_update_callback_config": {
    "callback_events": [
      "SHIPPING_ADDRESS"
    ],
    "callback_url": "http://example.com"
  }
}
```

Customizes the payer experience during the approval process for payment with PayPal.<blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> Partners and Marketplaces might configure <code>brand_name</code> and <code>shipping_preference</code> during partner account setup, which overrides the request values.</blockquote>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brand_name|string|false|none|The label that overrides the business name in the PayPal account on the PayPal site. The pattern is defined by an external party and supports Unicode.|
|locale|object|false|none|none|
|shipping_preference|string|false|none|The location from which the shipping address is derived.|
|contact_preference|string|false|none|The preference to display the contact information (buyer’s shipping email & phone number) on PayPal's checkout for easy merchant-buyer communication.|
|return_url|object|false|none|none|
|cancel_url|object|false|none|none|
|app_switch_context|object|false|none|none|
|landing_page|string|false|none|The type of landing page to show on the PayPal site for customer checkout.|
|user_action|string|false|none|Configures a <strong>Continue</strong> or <strong>Pay Now</strong> checkout flow.|
|payment_method_preference|string|false|none|The merchant-preferred payment methods.|
|order_update_callback_config|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|shipping_preference|GET_FROM_FILE|
|shipping_preference|NO_SHIPPING|
|shipping_preference|SET_PROVIDED_ADDRESS|
|contact_preference|NO_CONTACT_INFO|
|contact_preference|UPDATE_CONTACT_INFO|
|contact_preference|RETAIN_CONTACT_INFO|
|landing_page|LOGIN|
|landing_page|GUEST_CHECKOUT|
|landing_page|NO_PREFERENCE|
|landing_page|BILLING|
|user_action|CONTINUE|
|user_action|PAY_NOW|
|payment_method_preference|UNRESTRICTED|
|payment_method_preference|IMMEDIATE_PAYMENT_REQUIRED|

|usage|[stored_payment_source_usage_type](#schemastored_payment_source_usage_type)|false|none|Indicates if this is a `first` or `subsequent` payment using a stored payment source (also referred to as stored credential or card on file).|

|---|---|

|payment_initiator|MERCHANT|
|usage_pattern|IMMEDIATE|

|usage_pattern|RECURRING_POSTPAID|
|usage_pattern|THRESHOLD_PREPAID|
|usage_pattern|THRESHOLD_POSTPAID|
|usage_pattern|SUBSCRIPTION_PREPAID|
|usage_pattern|SUBSCRIPTION_POSTPAID|
|usage_pattern|UNSCHEDULED_PREPAID|
|usage_pattern|UNSCHEDULED_POSTPAID|
|usage_pattern|INSTALLMENT_PREPAID|
|usage_pattern|INSTALLMENT_POSTPAID|
|usage|FIRST|
|usage|SUBSEQUENT|
|usage|DERIVED|

<h2 id="tocS_phone_with_national_required_and_country_code">phone_with_national_required_and_country_code</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaphone_with_national_required_and_country_code"></a>
<a id="schema_phone_with_national_required_and_country_code"></a>

<a id="tocsphone_with_national_required_and_country_code"></a>

```json
{
  "country_code": "str",
  "national_number": "string"
}
```

A structured representation of a phone number conforming to the international [E.164 numbering plan format](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-E.164/en),requiring the national_number field and optionally supporting the country_code.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|country_code|string|false|none|The country calling code (CC), in its canonical international [E.164 numbering plan format](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-E.164/en). The combined length of the CC and the national number must not be greater than 15 digits. The national number consists of a national destination code (NDC) and subscriber number (SN).|
|national_number|string|true|none|The national number, in its canonical international [E.164 numbering plan format](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-E.164/en). The combined length of the country calling code (CC) and the national number must not be greater than 15 digits. The national number consists of a national destination code (NDC) and subscriber number (SN).|

### Properties

|card|object|true|none|Google Pay tokenized credit card used to pay.|
|authentication_method|string|true|none|Authentication Method which is used for the card transaction.|
|cryptogram|string|false|none|Base-64 cryptographic identifier used by card schemes to validate the token verification result. This is a conditionally required field if authentication_method is CRYPTOGRAM_3DS.|
|eci_indicator|string|false|none|Electronic Commerce Indicator may not always be present. It is only returned for tokens on the Visa card network. This value is passed through in the payment authorization request.|

|order_update_callback_config|object|false|none|none|
|user_action|string|false|none|Configures a <strong>Continue</strong> or <strong>Pay Now</strong> checkout flow.|

|Property|Value|

|user_action|PAY_NOW|


Resource consolidating common request and response attirbutes for vaulting Venmo Wallet.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|store_in_vault|[store_in_vault_instruction](#schemastore_in_vault_instruction)|true|none|Defines how and when the payment source gets vaulted.|
|description|string|false|none|The description displayed to Venmo consumer on the approval flow for Venmo, as well as on the Venmo payment token management experience on Venmo.com.|
|usage_pattern|string|false|none|Expected business/pricing model for the billing agreement.|
|usage_type|string|true|none|The usage type associated with the Venmo payment token.|
|customer_type|string|false|none|The customer type associated with the Venmo payment token. This is to indicate whether the customer acting on the merchant / platform is either a business or a consumer.|
|permit_multiple_payment_tokens|boolean|false|none|Create multiple payment tokens for the same payer, merchant/platform combination. Use this when the customer has not logged in at merchant/platform. The payment token thus generated, can then also be used to create the customer account at merchant/platform. Use this also when multiple payment tokens are required for the same payer, different customer at merchant/platform. This helps to identify customers distinctly even though they may share the same Venmo account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|store_in_vault|ON_SUCCESS|
|usage_pattern|IMMEDIATE|
|usage_pattern|DEFERRED|
|usage_pattern|RECURRING_PREPAID|
|usage_pattern|RECURRING_POSTPAID|
|usage_pattern|THRESHOLD_PREPAID|
|usage_pattern|THRESHOLD_POSTPAID|
|usage_type|MERCHANT|
|usage_type|PLATFORM|
|customer_type|CONSUMER|
|customer_type|BUSINESS|

<a id="tocspayment_method"></a>

```json
{
  "payee_preferred": "UNRESTRICTED",
  "standard_entry_class_code": "WEB"
}
```

The customer and merchant payment preferences.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payee_preferred|[payee_payment_method_preference](#schemapayee_payment_method_preference)|false|none|The merchant-preferred payment methods.|
|standard_entry_class_code|string|false|none|NACHA (the regulatory body governing the ACH network) requires that API callers (merchants, partners) obtain the consumer’s explicit authorization before initiating a transaction. To stay compliant, you’ll need to make sure that you retain a compliant authorization for each transaction that you originate to the ACH Network using this API. ACH transactions are categorized (using SEC codes) by how you capture authorization from the Receiver (the person whose bank account is being debited or credited). PayPal supports the following SEC codes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|payee_preferred|UNRESTRICTED|
|payee_preferred|IMMEDIATE_PAYMENT_REQUIRED|
|standard_entry_class_code|TEL|
|standard_entry_class_code|WEB|
|standard_entry_class_code|CCD|
|standard_entry_class_code|PPD|

<h2 id="tocS_stored_payment_source">stored_payment_source</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastored_payment_source"></a>
<a id="schema_stored_payment_source"></a>
<a id="tocSstored_payment_source"></a>
<a id="tocsstored_payment_source"></a>

```json
{
  "payment_initiator": "CUSTOMER",
  "payment_type": "ONE_TIME",
  "usage": "DERIVED",
  "previous_network_transaction_reference": {
    "id": "stringstr",
    "date": "stri",
    "network": {},
    "acquirer_reference_number": "string"
  }
}
```

Provides additional details to process a payment using a `payment_source` that has been stored or is intended to be stored (also referred to as stored_credential or card-on-file).<br/>Parameter compatibility:<br/><ul><li>`payment_type=ONE_TIME` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`usage=FIRST` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`previous_transaction_reference` or `previous_network_transaction_reference` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=MERCHANT`.</li><li>Only one of the parameters - `previous_transaction_reference` and `previous_network_transaction_reference` - can be present in the request.</li></ul>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_initiator|[payment_initiator](#schemapayment_initiator)|true|none|The person or party who initiated or triggered the payment.|
|payment_type|[stored_payment_source_payment_type](#schemastored_payment_source_payment_type)|true|none|Indicates the type of the stored payment_source payment.|
|usage|[stored_payment_source_usage_type](#schemastored_payment_source_usage_type)|false|none|Indicates if this is a `first` or `subsequent` payment using a stored payment source (also referred to as stored credential or card on file).|
|previous_network_transaction_reference|[network_transaction_reference](#schemanetwork_transaction_reference)|false|none|Reference values used by the card network to identify a transaction.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|payment_initiator|CUSTOMER|
|payment_initiator|MERCHANT|
|payment_type|ONE_TIME|
|payment_type|RECURRING|
|payment_type|UNSCHEDULED|
|usage|FIRST|
|usage|SUBSEQUENT|
|usage|DERIVED|

Customizes the payer experience during the approval process for the payment with PayPal.<blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> Partners and Marketplaces might configure <code>brand_name</code> and <code>shipping_preference</code> during partner account setup, which overrides the request values.</blockquote>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brand_name|string|false|none|DEPRECATED. The label that overrides the business name in the PayPal account on the PayPal site. The fields in `application_context` are now available in the `experience_context` object under the `payment_source` which supports them (eg. `payment_source.paypal.experience_context.brand_name`). Please specify this field in the `experience_context` object instead of the `application_context` object.|
|locale|object|false|none|none|
|landing_page|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED. DEPRECATED. The type of landing page to show on the PayPal site for customer checkout.  The fields in `application_context` are now available in the `experience_context` object under the `payment_source` which supports them (eg. `payment_source.paypal.experience_context.landing_page`). Please specify this field in the `experience_context` object instead of the `application_context` object. <b>DEPRECATED</b><br><table><tr><th>See</th><th>Since Version</th></tr><tr><td>payment_source.paypal.experience_context.landing_page</td><td>2.9</td></tr></table>|
|shipping_preference|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED. DEPRECATED. The shipping preference:<ul><li>Displays the shipping address to the customer.</li><li>Enables the customer to choose an address on the PayPal site.</li><li>Restricts the customer from changing the address during the payment-approval process.</li></ul>.  The fields in `application_context` are now available in the `experience_context` object under the `payment_source` which supports them (eg. `payment_source.paypal.experience_context.shipping_preference`). Please specify this field in the `experience_context` object instead of the `application_context` object. <b>DEPRECATED</b><br><table><tr><th>See</th><th>Since Version</th></tr><tr><td>payment_source.paypal.experience_context.shipping_preference</td><td>2.9</td></tr></table>|
|user_action|string|false|none|DEPRECATED. Configures a <strong>Continue</strong> or <strong>Pay Now</strong> checkout flow.  The fields in `application_context` are now available in the `experience_context` object under the `payment_source` which supports them (eg. `payment_source.paypal.experience_context.user_action`). Please specify this field in the `experience_context` object instead of the `application_context` object.|
|payment_method|object|false|none|none|
|return_url|string(uri)|false|none|DEPRECATED. The URL where the customer is redirected after the customer approves the payment. The fields in `application_context` are now available in the `experience_context` object under the `payment_source` which supports them (eg. `payment_source.paypal.experience_context.return_url`). Please specify this field in the `experience_context` object instead of the `application_context` object.|
|cancel_url|string(uri)|false|none|DEPRECATED. The URL where the customer is redirected after the customer cancels the payment. The fields in `application_context` are now available in the `experience_context` object under the `payment_source` which supports them (eg. `payment_source.paypal.experience_context.cancel_url`). Please specify this field in the `experience_context` object instead of the `application_context` object.|
|stored_payment_source|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|landing_page|LOGIN|
|landing_page|BILLING|
|landing_page|NO_PREFERENCE|
|shipping_preference|GET_FROM_FILE|
|shipping_preference|NO_SHIPPING|
|shipping_preference|SET_PROVIDED_ADDRESS|
|user_action|CONTINUE|
|user_action|PAY_NOW|

The order request details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|[checkout_payment_intent](#schemacheckout_payment_intent)|true|none|The intent to either capture payment immediately or authorize a payment for an order after order creation.|
|payer|object|false|none|none|
|purchase_units|[object]|true|none|An array of purchase units. Each purchase unit establishes a contract between a payer and the payee. Each purchase unit represents either a full or partial order that the payer intends to purchase from the payee.|
|payment_source|[payment_source](#schemapayment_source)|false|none|The payment source definition.|
|application_context|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|intent|CAPTURE|
|intent|AUTHORIZE|

|oneOf|[object]|false|none|An array of sub-schemas. The data must validate against one sub-schema.|
|not|object|false|none|Not.|
|links|[object]|false|read-only|An array of links.|

The request-related [HATEOAS link](/api/rest/responses/#hateoas-links) information.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|href|string|true|none|The complete target URL. To make the related call, combine the method with this [URI Template-formatted](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6570) link. For pre-processing, include the `$`, `(`, and `)` characters. The `href` is the key HATEOAS component that links a completed call with a subsequent call.|
|rel|string|true|none|The [link relation type](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5988#section-4), which serves as an ID for a link that unambiguously describes the semantics of the link. See [Link Relations](https://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/link-relations.xhtml).|
|method|string|false|none|The HTTP method required to make the related call.|
|title|string|false|none|The link title.|
|mediaType|string|false|none|The media type, as defined by [RFC 2046](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2046.txt). Describes the link target.|
|encType|string|false|none|The media type in which to submit the request data.|
|schema|object|false|none|none|
|targetSchema|object|false|none|none|

|---|---|
|method|GET|
|method|POST|
|method|PUT|
|method|DELETE|
|method|HEAD|
|method|CONNECT|
|method|OPTIONS|
|method|PATCH|

The error details. Required for client-side `4XX` errors.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|field|string|false|none|The field that caused the error. If this field is in the body, set this value to the field's JSON pointer value. Required for client-side errors.|
|value|string|false|none|The value of the field that caused the error.|
|location|string|false|none|The location of the field that caused the error. Value is `body`, `path`, or `query`.|
|issue|string|true|none|The unique, fine-grained application-level error code.|
|links|[object]|false|read-only|An array of request-related [HATEOAS links](/api/rest/responses/#hateoas-links) that are either relevant to the issue by providing additional information or offering potential resolutions.|
|description|string|false|none|The human-readable description for an issue. The description can change over the lifetime of an API, so clients must not depend on this value.|

|bin_details|object|false|none|none|
|stored_credential|[card_stored_credential](#schemacard_stored_credential)|false|none|Provides additional details to process a payment using a `card` that has been stored or is intended to be stored (also referred to as stored_credential or card-on-file).<br/>Parameter compatibility:<br/><ul><li>`payment_type=ONE_TIME` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`usage=FIRST` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`previous_transaction_reference` or `previous_network_transaction_reference` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=MERCHANT`.</li><li>Only one of the parameters - `previous_transaction_reference` and `previous_network_transaction_reference` - can be present in the request.</li></ul>|

Information needed to pay using ApplePay.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|ApplePay transaction identifier, this will be the unique identifier for this transaction provided by Apple. The pattern is defined by an external party and supports Unicode.|
|token|string|false|none|Encrypted ApplePay token, containing card information. This token would be base64encoded. The pattern is defined by an external party and supports Unicode.|
|name|object|false|none|none|
|email_address|object|false|none|none|
|phone_number|object|false|none|none|
|card|object|false|none|none|
|attributes|object|false|none|none|
|stored_credential|[card_stored_credential](#schemacard_stored_credential)|false|none|Provides additional details to process a payment using a `card` that has been stored or is intended to be stored (also referred to as stored_credential or card-on-file).<br/>Parameter compatibility:<br/><ul><li>`payment_type=ONE_TIME` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`usage=FIRST` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`previous_transaction_reference` or `previous_network_transaction_reference` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=MERCHANT`.</li><li>Only one of the parameters - `previous_transaction_reference` and `previous_network_transaction_reference` - can be present in the request.</li></ul>|

The payment source used to fund the payment.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card|[card_response](#schemacard_response)|false|none|The payment card to use to fund a payment. Card can be a credit or debit card.|
|paypal|[paypal_wallet_response](#schemapaypal_wallet_response)|false|none|The PayPal Wallet response.|
|bancontact|[bancontact](#schemabancontact)|false|none|Information used to pay Bancontact.|
|blik|[blik](#schemablik)|false|none|Information used to pay using BLIK.|
|eps|[eps](#schemaeps)|false|none|Information used to pay using eps.|
|giropay|[giropay](#schemagiropay)|false|none|Information needed to pay using giropay.|
|ideal|[ideal](#schemaideal)|false|none|Information used to pay using iDEAL.|
|mybank|[mybank](#schemamybank)|false|none|Information used to pay using MyBank.|
|p24|[p24](#schemap24)|false|none|Information used to pay using P24(Przelewy24).|
|sofort|[sofort](#schemasofort)|false|none|Information used to pay using Sofort.|
|trustly|[trustly](#schematrustly)|false|none|Information needed to pay using Trustly.|
|apple_pay|[apple_pay](#schemaapple_pay)|false|none|Information needed to pay using ApplePay.|
|google_pay|[google_pay](#schemagoogle_pay)|false|none|Google Pay Wallet payment data.|
|venmo|[venmo_wallet_response](#schemavenmo_wallet_response)|false|none|Venmo wallet response.|
|crypto|[crypto](#schemacrypto)|false|none|Pay With Crypto details response object.|

The details for the items to be purchased.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The item name or title.|
|unit_amount|object|true|none|none|
|tax|object|false|none|none|
|quantity|string|true|none|The item quantity. Must be a whole number.|
|description|string|false|none|The detailed item description.|
|sku|string|false|none|The stock keeping unit (SKU) for the item.|
|url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL to the item being purchased. Visible to buyer and used in buyer experiences.|
|category|string|false|none|The item category type.|
|image_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL of the item's image. File type and size restrictions apply. An image that violates these restrictions will not be honored.|
|upc|object|false|none|none|
|billing_plan|[order_billing_plan](#schemaorder_billing_plan)|false|none|Metadata for merchant-managed recurring billing plans. Valid only during the saved payment method token or billing agreement creation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|category|DIGITAL_GOODS|
|category|PHYSICAL_GOODS|
|category|DONATION|

The request-related [HATEOAS link](/api/rest/responses/#hateoas-links) information.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|href|string|true|none|The complete target URL. To make the related call, combine the method with this [URI Template-formatted](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6570) link. For pre-processing, include the `$`, `(`, and `)` characters. The `href` is the key HATEOAS component that links a completed call with a subsequent call.|
|rel|string|true|none|The [link relation type](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5988#section-4), which serves as an ID for a link that unambiguously describes the semantics of the link. See [Link Relations](https://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/link-relations.xhtml).|
|method|string|false|none|The HTTP method required to make the related call.|
|title|string|false|none|The link title.|
|mediaType|string|false|none|The media type, as defined by [RFC 2046](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2046.txt). Describes the link target.|
|encType|string|false|none|The media type in which to submit the request data.|
|schema|object|false|none|none|
|targetSchema|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|method|GET|
|method|POST|
|method|PUT|
|method|DELETE|
|method|HEAD|


The collection of payments, or transactions, for a purchase unit in an order. For example, authorized payments, captured payments, and refunds.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authorizations|[object]|false|none|An array of authorized payments for a purchase unit. A purchase unit can have zero or more authorized payments.|
|captures|[object]|false|none|An array of captured payments for a purchase unit. A purchase unit can have zero or more captured payments.|
|refunds|[object]|false|none|An array of refunds for a purchase unit. A purchase unit can have zero or more refunds.|


The purchase unit details. Used to capture required information for the payment contract.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|reference_id|string|false|none|The API caller-provided external ID for the purchase unit. Required for multiple purchase units when you must update the order through `PATCH`. If you omit this value and the order contains only one purchase unit, PayPal sets this value to `default`. <blockquote><strong>Note:</strong> If there are multiple purchase units, <code>reference_id</code> is required for each purchase unit.</blockquote>|
|amount|[amount_with_breakdown](#schemaamount_with_breakdown)|false|none|The total order amount with an optional breakdown that provides details, such as the total item amount, total tax amount, shipping, handling, insurance, and discounts, if any.<br/>If you specify `amount.breakdown`, the amount equals `item_total` plus `tax_total` plus `shipping` plus `handling` plus `insurance` minus `shipping_discount` minus discount.<br/>The amount must be a positive number. For listed of supported currencies and decimal precision, see the PayPal REST APIs <a href="/docs/integration/direct/rest/currency-codes/">Currency Codes</a>.|
|payee|object|false|none|none|
|payment_instruction|[payment_instruction](#schemapayment_instruction)|false|none|Any additional payment instructions to be consider during payment processing. This processing instruction is applicable for Capturing an order or Authorizing an Order.|
|description|string|false|none|The purchase description.|
|custom_id|string|false|none|The API caller-provided external ID. Used to reconcile API caller-initiated transactions with PayPal transactions. Appears in transaction and settlement reports.|
|invoice_id|string|false|none|The API caller-provided external invoice ID for this order.|
|id|string|false|none|The PayPal-generated ID for the purchase unit. This ID appears in both the payer's transaction history and the emails that the payer receives. In addition, this ID is available in transaction and settlement reports that merchants and API callers can use to reconcile transactions. This ID is only available when an order is saved by calling <code>v2/checkout/orders/id/save</code>.|
|soft_descriptor|string|false|none|The payment descriptor on account transactions on the customer's credit card statement, that PayPal sends to processors. The maximum length of the soft descriptor information that you can pass in the API field is 22 characters, in the following format:<code>22 - len(PAYPAL * (8)) - len(<var>Descriptor in Payment Receiving Preferences of Merchant account</var> + 1)</code>The PAYPAL prefix uses 8 characters.<br/><br/>The soft descriptor supports the following ASCII characters:<ul><li>Alphanumeric characters</li><li>Dashes</li><li>Asterisks</li><li>Periods (.)</li><li>Spaces</li></ul>For Wallet payments marketplace integrations:<ul><li>The merchant descriptor in the Payment Receiving Preferences must be the marketplace name.</li><li>You can't use the remaining space to show the customer service number.</li><li>The remaining spaces can be a combination of seller name and country.</li></ul><br/>For unbranded payments (Direct Card) marketplace integrations, use a combination of the seller name and phone number.|
|items|[object]|false|none|An array of items that the customer purchases from the merchant.|
|shipping|object|false|none|none|
|supplementary_data|object|false|none|none|
|payments|object|false|none|none|

The order details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|create_time|object|false|none|none|
|update_time|object|false|none|none|
|id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the order.|
|payment_source|object|false|none|none|
|intent|object|false|none|none|
|payer|object|false|none|none|
|purchase_units|[object]|false|none|An array of purchase units. Each purchase unit establishes a contract between a customer and merchant. Each purchase unit represents either a full or partial order that the customer intends to purchase from the merchant.|
|status|object|false|none|none|
|links|[object]|false|read-only|An array of request-related HATEOAS links. To complete payer approval, use the `approve` link to redirect the payer. The API caller has 6 hours (default setting, this which can be changed by your account manager to 24/48/72 hours to accommodate your use case) from the time the order is created, to redirect your payer. Once redirected, the API caller has 6 hours for the payer to approve the order and either authorize or capture the order. If you are not using the PayPal JavaScript SDK to initiate PayPal Checkout (in context) ensure that you include `application_context.return_url` is specified or you will get "We're sorry, Things don't appear to be working at the moment" after the payer approves the payment.|

<h2 id="tocS_patch">patch</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapatch"></a>
<a id="schema_patch"></a>
<a id="tocSpatch"></a>
<a id="tocspatch"></a>

```json
{
  "op": "add",
  "path": "string",
  "value": null,
  "from": "string"
}
```

The JSON patch object to apply partial updates to resources.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|op|string|true|none|The operation.|
|path|string|false|none|The <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901">JSON Pointer</a> to the target document location at which to complete the operation.|
|value|object|false|none|The value to apply. The <code>remove</code>, <code>copy</code>, and <code>move</code> operations do not require a value. Since <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6902">JSON Patch</a> allows any type for <code>value</code>, the <code>type</code> property is not specified.|
|from|string|false|none|The <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901">JSON Pointer</a> to the target document location from which to move the value. Required for the <code>move</code> operation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|op|add|
|op|remove|
|op|replace|
|op|move|
|op|copy|
|op|test|

Customizes the payer confirmation experience.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brand_name|string|false|none|Label to present to your payer as part of the PayPal hosted web experience.|
|locale|object|false|none|none|
|return_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where the customer is redirected after the customer approves the payment.|
|cancel_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where the customer is redirected after the customer cancels the payment.|
|stored_payment_source|[stored_payment_source](#schemastored_payment_source)|false|none|Provides additional details to process a payment using a `payment_source` that has been stored or is intended to be stored (also referred to as stored_credential or card-on-file).<br/>Parameter compatibility:<br/><ul><li>`payment_type=ONE_TIME` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`usage=FIRST` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=CUSTOMER`.</li><li>`previous_transaction_reference` or `previous_network_transaction_reference` is compatible only with `payment_initiator=MERCHANT`.</li><li>Only one of the parameters - `previous_transaction_reference` and `previous_network_transaction_reference` - can be present in the request.</li></ul>|

Payer confirms the intent to pay for the Order using the provided payment source.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_source|[payment_source](#schemapayment_source)|true|none|The payment source definition.|
|application_context|[order_confirm_application_context](#schemaorder_confirm_application_context)|false|none|Customizes the payer confirmation experience.|

The order authorize response.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|create_time|object|false|none|none|
|update_time|object|false|none|none|
|id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the order.|
|payment_source|object|false|none|none|
|intent|object|false|none|none|
|payer|object|false|none|none|
|purchase_units|[object]|false|none|An array of purchase units. Each purchase unit establishes a contract between a customer and merchant. Each purchase unit represents either a full or partial order that the customer intends to purchase from the merchant.|
|status|object|false|none|none|
|links|[object]|false|read-only|An array of request-related HATEOAS links. To complete payer approval, use the `approve` link to redirect the payer. The API caller has 6 hours (default setting, this which can be changed by your account manager to 24/48/72 hours to accommodate your use case) from the time the order is created, to redirect your payer. Once redirected, the API caller has 6 hours for the payer to approve the order and either authorize or capture the order. If you are not using the PayPal JavaScript SDK to initiate PayPal Checkout (in context) ensure that you include `application_context.return_url` is specified or you will get "We're sorry, Things don't appear to be working at the moment" after the payer approves the payment.|

<h2 id="tocS_shipment_carrier">shipment_carrier</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemashipment_carrier"></a>
<a id="schema_shipment_carrier"></a>
<a id="tocSshipment_carrier"></a>
<a id="tocsshipment_carrier"></a>

```json
"DPD_RU"
```

The carrier for the shipment. Some carriers have a global version as well as local subsidiaries. The subsidiaries are repeated over many countries and might also have an entry in the global list. Choose the carrier for your country. If the carrier is not available for your country, choose the global version of the carrier. If your carrier name is not in the list, set `carrier` to `OTHER` and set carrier name in `carrier_name_other`. For allowed values, see <a href="/docs/tracking/reference/carriers/">Carriers</a>.
